heading, The world's leading hospitals are breaking down communication barriers, level 2
heading, See how teams are providing equality of experience for patients, consistency of service for providers and efficiency of outcomes for hospitals through improved communication., level 6
Epsom and St Helier reduces avoidable readmissions in maternity services with CardMedic

ESTH implemented CardMedic as part of its digital transformation strategy to address communication barriers, ensuring non-English-speaking patients receive critical information in their preferred language before discharge.
end of link, View Case Study
Enhancing neonatal care at a leading London NHS trust

The neonatal unit at one of the leading London NHS trusts in the UK is using CardMedic to reassure new families that have additional communication needs that their newborn babies are being looked after, improving trust between families and care teams.
end of link, View Case Study
Not-for-profit, community based Nor-Lea Hospital District in Lovington, New Mexico, is using CardMedic to reduce the risk of communication errors with patients.
end of link, View Case Study
The Christie, Leading European Cancer Care Hospital
The Christie, can now make sure every patient with additional communication needs receives the best possible person centred care, reducing health inequalities for often underserved patients.
end of link, View Case Study
University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust evaluates CardMedic
of CardMedic in the trust’s maternity department. Deployed across the Leicester
General Hospital and Leicester Royal Infirmary, the trust has used CardMedic to help
break down communication barriers for pregnant women and birthing people with
additional communication needs to deliver more equitable care
end of link, View Case Study
How CardMedic helped the Patel family receive more equitable maternity care from North East London Health and Care Partnership
CardMedic is helping families feel listened to throughout their maternity journey by empowering them to communicate with their care teams.
end of link, View Case Study
How CardMedic combined grant funding and R&D Tax Credits to scale innovation across the NHS

CardMedic scaled across nearly 30 NHS trusts by combining nearly £1m in Innovate UK and SBRI grant funding (secured with Venturenomix) with R&D Tax Credits (delivered by Leyton), preserving ownership while extending the financial runway needed to prove clinical and commercial value within the NHS.
end of link, View Case Study
